current_phase.next_action: Module implemented and verified. Remaining follow-up is optional manual browser walkthrough on a real trip if visual confirmation is desired.

audit_findings.finding: reservations.itinerary_item_id is declared (line 78) as a nullable foreignId on itinerary_items with nullOnDelete, but no code path ever assigns it. The column is dead weight and is dropped in Phase 01.

store() and update() already wrap reservation writes in DB::transaction. syncReservationDetails() is the existing junction-table sync (flight_segments, lodging_stays, flight_details). Phase 02 appends syncTripDaySpan() to this method so pivot writes ride the same transaction with zero possibility of drift.
Fillable contains 'itinerary_item_id'; itineraryItem() BelongsTo is defined. Both are removed in Phase 01 in favor of tripDays() BelongsToMany.
reservation() HasOne is defined but never called by any meaningful code path. Removed in Phase 01.

Trip serializer eager-loads reservations.* via the top-level chain and renders the Reservations tab from there. Phase 03 adds parallel days.reservations eager loads plus a smaller per-day card shape on each days[*] entry. The top-level trip.reservations payload is untouched.

Itinerary tab iterates day.items (ItineraryItem rows only). Reservations live in a separate tab block starting near line 1594. Phase 04 inserts a new day.reservations render block between day.items and day.tasks; reservations stay non-editable on the itinerary tab and deep-link to the Reservations tab card via id=reservation-{id}.
trips.destination_timezone exists. It is the primary timezone for the day-span computation in Reservation::computeOverlappingDates(), with a fallback chain to reservation.starts_timezone then UTC.
Existing focus-target convention for jumping to a specific entity on the trip page. Phase 04's openReservation() helper mirrors this pattern but for an in-page tab switch.

decisions_locked_in: Reservations ARE itinerary entries. No auto-created mirror ItineraryItem rows. The itinerary tab queries reservations directly via the trip_day_reservation pivot.
Multi-day rendering = every day in the date range. Lodging excludes the check-out day (you sleep on nights 12-14, not on day 15). Encoded in Reservation::computeOverlappingDates().

Backfill via migration. A second migration walks every existing reservation with a non-null starts_at and inserts its pivot rows using the same computeOverlappingDates() helper that the runtime sync uses.
Itinerary-tab reservation entries are read-only. Editing happens on the Reservations tab. The 'Open' button on a day-card entry deep-links to the matching reservation card via id and tabindex focus.
The dead reservations.itinerary_item_id column is dropped, not kept as a legacy nullable. Both Eloquent relations (Reservation::itineraryItem, ItineraryItem::reservation) are removed.
Timezone fallback chain for the day-span calc: trips.destination_timezone -> reservation.starts_timezone -> UTC. Matches the convention set by the trip-timezones module.
No new activity event type. Existing reservation.created / reservation.updated / reservation.deleted events already cover live-collaboration refresh via activity_version polling.
Pivot table name: trip_day_reservation. The Eloquent belongsToMany relations declare the table name explicitly to match the locked migration contract.
day_index / day_total / spans_multiple_days computed server-side and shipped on each per-day reservation card payload. Frontend never re-derives.

Within a single day, day.reservations sort by starts_at ASC then id ASC. Items + reservations are NOT interleaved by time in this module; they render as two grouped blocks (items first, then reservations). Interleaving is a follow-up if requested.
Trip timezone changes after the fact do not auto-resync pivots. The user must touch each reservation to trigger a resync. Documented limitation; revisit only if it surfaces in practice.

store.name: trips.reservations.store
store.change: Inside the existing DB::transaction, after syncReservationDetails() returns, syncTripDaySpan() runs. The pivot rows always commit atomically with the reservation row.

update.name: trips.reservations.update
update.change: Same as store. Updates that shrink the date span call $reservation->tripDays()->sync($ids) (NOT syncWithoutDetaching) so abandoned day rows are removed.

destroy.name: trips.reservations.destroy
destroy.change: No controller change. Pivot rows cascade via FK cascadeOnDelete on trip_day_reservation.reservation_id.

show_payload.name: trips.show
show_payload.change: days[*] gains a 'reservations' array. Shape: { id, type, title, provider_name, status, starts_at, starts_timezone, ends_at, ends_timezone, location_name, spans_multiple_days, day_index, day_total }. Sorted by starts_at ASC then id ASC. Top-level trip.reservations payload is unchanged.

state_owners.pivot_truth: trip_day_reservation table. Unique on (trip_day_id, reservation_id). Cascade-delete on both FKs.
state_owners.date_span_logic: Reservation::computeOverlappingDates(Trip $trip) — the single location for the lodging exclusion and the timezone fallback chain. Called by the runtime sync (Phase 02) and the backfill migration (Phase 05).
state_owners.per_day_reservation_list: Server-computed in TripController::show. Emitted as days[*].reservations. Sorted server-side. Frontend never re-derives.
state_owners.top_level_reservation_list: Unchanged. trip.reservations remains the source for the Reservations tab card list.
state_owners.itinerary_tab_render_state: Vue template iterates day.reservations after day.items. No local form state. No editable controls.
state_owners.deep_link_focus_state: openReservation(id) helper in Trips/Show.vue. Switches activePanel to 'reservations', then reuses focusDeepLinkedElement() to scroll and focus #reservation-{id}. Matches the notification-deep-links convention.

ux_rules.day_card_layout: Reservation entries render below day.items and above day.tasks (when present). Dashed border + muted background + 'Reservation' badge distinguish them from free-form items.
ux_rules.type_icons: Lucide icons per type: flight=Plane, lodging=BedDouble, transport=Car, activity=Ticket, dining=Utensils, default=CalendarClock.
ux_rules.multi_day_label: Lodging entries show 'Night N of M'; non-lodging multi-day entries show 'Day N of M'. Hidden when day_total === 1.
ux_rules.open_button: Single 'Open' button per entry. No Edit, no Delete on the itinerary tab. Click switches to the Reservations tab and scrolls/focuses the matching card.
ux_rules.empty_state: The day-card empty-state guard becomes v-if="day.items.length || day.tasks.length || day.reservations.length". A day with only a reservation hides the empty state.
ux_rules.unscheduled_reservations: Reservations with starts_at = null produce zero pivot rows and appear on zero itinerary day cards. They remain visible on the Reservations tab. This is intentional.
ux_rules.shared_trip_attribution: Itinerary-tab reservation entries do NOT show 'Last edited by'. The full Reservations tab card already exposes this.

verification.notes: Final run passed with no dirty PHP formatting changes.
No runtime references remain to itinerary_item_id, Reservation::itineraryItem, or ItineraryItem::reservation.

handoff.summary: Implemented and verified. Reservations now sync to trip days through trip_day_reservation, existing reservations were backfilled locally, trip show payload emits days[*].reservations, and the itinerary tab renders read-only reservation cards with Open deep-links to the Reservations tab.
next_agent_steps: Optional: perform the Phase 05 manual browser workflow on a real trip to visually confirm the day-card rendering and smooth-scroll focus behavior.
Known limitation remains: trip timezone changes after reservations exist do not automatically resync pivots until each reservation is edited.
